chunks: With this chain of narrators, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-abi al-Sabah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and mention the Name of Allah in known days». He said: They are the days of al-Tashriq.

key_terms.أَيَّامٍ مَّعْدُودَاتٍ: Known days (specifically referring to the days of al-Tashriq)
key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of al-Tashriq (the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah)
key_terms.وَيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ: And they mention the Name of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the 'known days' mentioned in the Quran for remembering Allah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'known days' (ayyam ma'dudat) in Surah al-Hajj refer specifically to the Days of al-Tashriq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah). This identification underscores the ritual significance of these days for pilgrims, linking the Quranic command to remember Allah with the specific practice of *dhikr* and continued sacrifice after the main Hajj rites.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	With this chain of narrators, from Hussain bin Sa’eed, from Muhammed bin Fudail, from Abu’l-Sabah, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,
with regards to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «and mention the Name of Allah in known days» [22:28]. He said: They are the days of the easternization.
